svg.text: Test setup for step 3. Only the laptop USB is needed: the sensor takes 5 V from the Nucleo 5V pin.
USB cable to the laptop (power and code)
the two round transducers face the dog
ECHO: Nucleo D9 · PD15 (after the divider)
Sensor: VCC column 22, Trig 23, Echo 24, Gnd 25
Echo gives 5 V; an STM32 pin wants 3.3 V.
1 kΩ from Echo to PD15, 2 kΩ from PD15
Trig needs no resistor: 3.3 V is enough
1. Wire everything with the USB unplugged.
2. VCC on 5 V: the HC-SR04 does not work on 3.3 V.
3. Never connect Echo straight to the Nucleo.
4. Keep the front clear (range 2 cm to 4 m).
5. Feeder: an animal under 40 cm starts a photo.
6. Check every Nucleo pin label before plugging.
Kibbly hardware · circuit 3 of the circuits by part · wires U1 to U7 in hardware/04_wiring_list.md section 8
